text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish police are reducing surveillance of the feuding Hells Angels and Bandidos biker gangs after two months without any major incident and amid hopes of peace in the turf conflict which was sparked by shootings at Copenhagen International Airport in March 1996.

--The Danish government's draft 1998 state budget, to be unveiled in late August, is expected to include measures to combat fraud and cheating with social benefits, with companies to pay sick leave for three weeks before the public sector steps in to foot the bill.
--Enquiries into political scandals in Denmark are to be conducted in full openness with public access in future and not held in secret sessions behind closed doors as some politicians are urging.

--Danish biotechnogical group Novo Nordisk hopes to commercially exploit its sponsorship of the XV FIGO World Congress of Gynaecology & Obstetrics, which was held in Copenhagen this week, with plans for a major promotion of its hormone products in the American market.

--Green's first political opinion poll after the summer holiday shows that a centre-right grouping comprising Conservatives and Liberals would win power if elections were held today. It also indicates that a narrow majority of Danes would vote in favour of the European Union's Amsterdam treaty reforms. Denmark is to hold a referendum on EU next year, with general elections due in September 1998 at the latest.
